Schedule Send, Confidential Mode, Signatures, and Vacation Replies

Schedule messages for later, protect sensitive messages with confidential mode, add a professional signature, and set up a vacation responder when you're away.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Schedule a message to send later, find it in Scheduled, and cancel the send
  • ✓Send a message in confidential mode and explain what it does and does not prevent
  • ✓Create a signature and set it as the default for new messages and replies
  • ✓Turn on the vacation responder for a date range and know how to end it

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Schedule a message

On the job

You handle the office mailbox at Parkview Property Management.

Denise likes owner reports to arrive Monday morning, even when you finish them on a Wednesday. Priya needs a heads-up about suspicious bank details without that message getting forwarded around. And you'll be away at a training next week, so people who email you need to know whom to contact.

Your task: Use Gmail's sending options and settings so your mail works even when you aren't at your desk.

  1. Write the message as usual.
  2. Instead of selecting Send, select the arrow next to Send (More send options), then Schedule send.
  3. Choose one of the suggested times, or select Pick date & time, set the date and time, and select Schedule send.
  4. To check it, open Scheduled in the main menu (under More). The message waits there until it goes out.
  5. To stop it, open the message in Scheduled and select Cancel send. The message goes back to Drafts so you can edit it or send it now.
You can have up to 100 scheduled messages at a time. A scheduled message may go out a few minutes after the time you picked, and it's sent according to the time zone you chose when you scheduled it.

Confidential mode

Confidential mode adds limits to a message. Recipients can't forward, copy and paste, print, or download the message text and attachments, and you can make the message expire. To use it, select Toggle confidential mode (the lock with a clock) at the bottom of the compose window, choose an expiration date, choose whether recipients need an SMS passcode, and select Save.

Confidential mode is not a lock. Recipients can still take screenshots or photos of the message. Don't treat it as permission to email information your office's policy says shouldn't be emailed at all, such as full bank account or Social Security numbers.

Your signature

A signature is the text added to the end of your messages: your name, title, company, and work phone. In Gmail on a computer, open Settings (gear) › See all settings. On the General tab, scroll to Signature, create your signature, and type the text. You can set a default signature for new emails and another for replies and forwards. Select Save Changes at the bottom of the page. A signature can be up to 10,000 characters, and images count toward that limit.

💡 While writing a message, the Insert signature button (a pen) at the bottom of the compose window lets you switch signatures or remove the signature from that one message.

The vacation responder

The vacation responder sends an automatic reply while you're away. Open Settings › See all settings. On the General tab, find Vacation responder and select Vacation responder on. Enter the first day, an optional last day, a subject, and a message, and choose whether only people in your Contacts get the reply. Select Save Changes.

  • Most people get the automatic reply only the first time they email you. If they write again more than four days later and the responder is still on, they get it again.
  • To stop it early, select End now on the banner across the top of your inbox.
  • If you set a last day, it ends at 11:59 PM that day.
  • A good away message says when you'll be back and whom to contact instead. Don't announce that your home is empty or share personal details.
Outlook calls this feature automatic replies. The idea is the same: dates, a message, and an option to limit replies to people you know.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Use your own Gmail account for these steps, and send practice messages only to yourself.

  1. Create a signature with your name and the line “BEOC Office Assistant student”. Set it as the default for new emails and select Save Changes.
  2. Compose a message to yourself and schedule it for tomorrow morning. Open Scheduled and take a screenshot. Then cancel the send.
  3. Compose a message to yourself in confidential mode that expires in 1 day. Send it, open it from your inbox, and notice what's missing (for example, the Forward option).
  4. Turn on the vacation responder for any future date range with a short professional message. Take a screenshot of the settings, then turn it off and select Save Changes.
Deliverable: Submit your three screenshots (Scheduled, the confidential message, and the vacation responder settings) to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Gmail, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
